claims.statement: The access-by-design date is real and near: Article 3(1) applies to products and related services placed on the market after 12 September 2026.
Qualifying micro and small manufacturers are exempt from Chapter II, with specified linked-enterprise and subcontractor exceptions and a temporary newly-medium exception.

The opportunity is bounded to telemetry and metadata already retrieved or readily obtainable without disproportionate effort; the Act does not force creation of new telemetry or disclosure of derived insights.
The gateway must implement OEM decisions on identity, GDPR basis, trade-secret safeguards and safety restrictions rather than independently deciding disclosure rights.
Existing Azure and Cumulocity functions make platform bundling a credible response and weaken a generic API-only product.
AWS's published IoT pricing shows that raw connectivity and messaging are a small fraction of 2-6 PLN per device per month at scale.
A defensible price must therefore attach to field classification, entitlement, adapters, release tests, request logs, support and risk transfer rather than cloud transport.
Open W3C descriptions make the generic schema and interaction layer reproducible, while current EU standardisation work indicates continuing cross-sector semantic and interface gaps.
Cyber Resilience Act timing adds security-reporting and product-security work around the same launch window, raising delivery burden but not making a scoped gateway impossible.
The number of non-exempt OEM buyers, their internal-build quotes, procurement cycles and willingness to place an external gateway in the release path are not established.
Integrator distribution and a path to 30 recurring OEMs are not established.

contrary_evidence: The micro- and small-enterprise exemption materially narrows the stated target market.
Only readily available product and related-service data are in scope; new telemetry and derived insights are not automatically required.
Azure and Cumulocity already contain much of the underlying identity, API, data and fleet stack.
AWS demonstrates that commodity infrastructure cost does not support the proposed per-device price by itself.
W3C standards make generic Thing metadata and interaction descriptions readily reproducible.
GDPR, trade secrets, safety and Cyber Resilience Act obligations increase customer-specific review and liability.
